title: Swift 6 actor-isolation warnings in CentralManager.swift
description:
`flutter build macos` and `flutter build ios` emit three warnings at CentralManager.swift:206 and :382 that become compile errors under Swift 6:

```
CentralManager.swift:206:28: warning: actor-isolated property 'peripheral' cannot be accessed from outside of the actor
    let peripheral = actor.peripheral
                     ~~~~~~^~~~~~~~~~
                     await

CentralManager.swift:382:9: warning: actor-isolated property 'peripheral' can not be referenced from a nonisolated context
    lhs.peripheral == rhs.peripheral
        ^

CentralManager.swift:382:27: warning: actor-isolated property 'peripheral' can not be referenced from a nonisolated context
    lhs.peripheral == rhs.peripheral
                          ^
```

Surfaced during burn skill Mac↔iPad verification (butane_flutter-cip.1). Not blocking BLE flow today (15/15 PASS) but the project will stop building on Swift 6 without fixes.

Fix approaches:
- Line 206: add `await` when reading `actor.peripheral` from an async context, or make the accessor nonisolated.
- Line 382 (Equatable on PeripheralActor wrapper?): compare by a nonisolated identity field (e.g. `identifier`/`UUID`) instead of `peripheral` — equality shouldn't require actor hopping.
close_reason: Fixed by marking PeripheralActor.peripheral as nonisolated let — it's a constant set at init, never mutated, so actor isolation is unnecessary. Eliminates all three Swift 6 actor-isolation warnings at lines 200, 206, and 382 of CentralManager.swift.

value: BlueZ 5.72 central cannot force LE/GATT on dual-mode public-addressed peers (Mac/iPhone advertising with the same address used for BR/EDR) through D-Bus alone. select_conn_bearer in src/device.c breaks ties toward BR/EDR, bluetoothd tries HFP/AVDTP, ServicesResolved never flips. Device1.ConnectProfile(uuid) is BR/EDR-only in 5.72 (runs SDP, not ATT). PreferredBearer property landed in 5.80+ and only biases reconnects. The ONLY deterministic fix is ControllerMode = le in /etc/bluetooth/main.conf + systemctl restart bluetooth. bluetoothd applies it via MGMT_OP_SET_BREDR as root at init; user code needs no privileged API at runtime. Documented in docs/linux-dev-environment.md. For butane_flutter Linux central <-> Mac peripheral burns this is a hard prerequisite.

Linux BlueZ: the bluez 0.1.4 Dart package supports Central role only. Advertising (BlueZAdvertisement), GATT server (GattManager1/RegisterApplication), and characteristic notifications (startNotify/stopNotify) are NOT exposed by the public API. Must implement via raw D-Bus objects using dbus package for peripheral-role work (8h5.6, 8h5.7). Notifications for central role (8h5.5) also require raw D-Bus.

When ssh'd into Mac Studio from another Mac (e.g. MacBook) and running local-network commands (ssh to laptop, ping LAN hosts), macOS's Local Network permission will silently block connections with 'No route to host' — because the permission prompt appears on the Studio's console where the SSH user can't see it. Symptom indistinguishable from the target host being offline. Fix: physically walk to the Studio and approve, or pre-approve via System Settings → Privacy & Security → Local Network.

android-api31-bluetooth-scan-neverlocation: On Android 12+ (API 31+), BLUETOOTH_SCAN without android:usesPermissionFlags='neverForLocation' silently returns zero scan results when ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION is not granted. No onScanFailed is called — onScannerRegistered fires successfully and startScan returns, but onScanResult is never invoked. Fix: add neverForLocation to BLUETOOTH_SCAN in both the plugin manifest (packages/butane_android/android/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml) and the harness app manifest. Confirmed on API 36 (Android 16).

Never use .then/.catchError/.onError in Dart (this repo = butane_flutter). Use async/await with try/catch. For fire-and-forget Futures, wrap an async IIFE in unawaited(...): unawaited(() async { try { await someFuture(); } catch (err) { /* handle */ } }()). DO NOT write someFuture().then(...) or someFuture().catchError(...). Per explicit user instruction.

fs-agent-qwen36-critique-rogue-implementation: When fs deliberate dispatches a critique via fs_agent backed by qwen3.6-moe on swift-infer, the model has on multiple occasions ignored its grading mandate and instead IMPLEMENTED the bead under review — writing/editing source files in the live repo and auto-committing each tool call as a 'wip: write_file ...' commit directly on the active branch (main in this repo). It also runs aggressive cleanup like 'git checkout -- .beads/interactions.jsonl' and 'rm -f .beads/issues.jsonl', destroying staged/uncommitted work. Symptom: fs deliberate bg task produces nus.dart/scenarios/etc files and 'wip: ...' commits instead of returning the JSON envelope array. Architect at 2026-05-19 02:15 on bead 1a2 already noted the same model 'recovered from its earlier 413 and wrote a competing design' — same failure pattern. Mitigation: prefer subagent dispatch (Agent tool with subagent_type=critique) over fs_agent; or pin fs_agent to a different model. Recovery if it fires: 'git reset --hard <origin/main HEAD>' to drop the wip: commits (they're local-only), then restore any swept-up beads files from the rogue commit's tree before reset.
